summary: Implemented the deterministic offline acceptance-criteria checker introduced by T009. The checker parses every todo/phases/**/T[0-9]{3}.md with the Python standard library and fails closed on three rule families: acceptance-present (missing/empty Acceptance section or one with no falsifiable condition: no verification surface, no explicit pass/fail, and no rejection/refusal/invalid-input condition), acceptance-placeholder (a closed placeholder marker in Acceptance: TBD, TODO, to be determined, as appropriate, if possible), and acceptance-quantitative (a comparison phrase from the closed vocabulary that appears in Deliverables but never in Acceptance; the two grounded examples are the 5-minute USDG return <= -80% and the 5-minute return above 100%). The closed vocabulary (verification surfaces, explicit outcome terms, placeholder markers, comparison operators, unit terms) is committed beside the check and printed with every finding so a reviewer can re-derive every match by hand. The exception list is the same docs/implement/ci/suppressions.toml file T005 and T006 already share; T009 scopes its suppression-unused check to its own rule family names so T005/T006 entries never leak across checkers. Five pre-existing findings against contracts T000, T023, T092, and T009 (self-reference for the two historical cases) are recorded as suppressions with the required rule/reason/owner/expiry fields and a 2026-12-31 expiry. The check is wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml as a strictly additive required check between the T006 step and the ruff/mypy gates. The committed repository passes the check; exit code 0 on a passing repo, exit code 1 when any of the regression fixtures is run.

residual_risks: Two pre-existing test failures unrelated to T009 remain on this worktree: test_abi_artifacts.py::test_artifact_byte_matches_regenerated_oracle_output (Foundry vendored sources absent) and test_documentation_citations.py::test_check_passes_on_real_repository (a stale T005 citation finding on docs/implement/DOCUMENTATION_INTEGRITY_AUDIT.md:242 about storage.schema). T009 is not the contract owner for either and does not edit the surfaces they touch.

The four pre-existing acceptance-present findings against T000, T023, T092 and the two acceptance-quantitative findings against T009 (its own Deliverables quoting the two historical cases) are suppressed with a 2026-12-31 expiry. A reviewer who wants those contracts to pass the bare check without the suppression must amend the contract text; the T009 contract explicitly forbids editing the other contracts to silence findings, so the suppression carries the obligation forward.

The closed vocabulary is wider than the minimal five phrases each rule list could carry (e.g. tests/test_, test_, tests, test, test, tested, and the word 'command' are all accepted as verification surfaces). Widening is permitted by the contract; the reviewer can inspect tools/check_acceptance/vocabulary.py to confirm no entry was added to mask a contract already in the repo. The vocabulary cannot be narrowed, emptied or shortened to make a finding pass.
